svg.aria-label: What Null keeps. Under ~/Library/Application Support/io.github.dominionism.null-mini/ settings.json: Window position, chosen model, saved session ID, Full Disk Access prompt state, whether the first opening has happened, backup order, your own harness if you chose it, whether the pet shows, whether computer use is switched on, the thinking level you last set with /effort, the model you named to verify answers, and whether the browser link is on and Chrome was seen to load it history.json: A title for each conversation made in the box: the first line of its first message, at most 80 characters, since OMP gives none for these. Any title you gave with /rename. And, while there are any, which conversations are working or not yet looked at: an id and one word each, so that work cut off by a restart is found again routing.json: What each of the last 500 replies cost, in numbers: how many steps it took, how many of them failed, how long it ran, when it ended and how, the model and its thinking level, whether the conversation was in the box's own folder, and whether the reply was a second model verifying. No word that was typed, shown or read, and no conversation's id or title. Nothing is done with the numbers yet, and they do not leave this Mac harness.yml: Settings handed to OMP at every start: no update check, your backup order when there is one, and computer use on or off once you have used its switch. Rewritten each time rules.md: While computer use or the browser link is on: Null's own rules for each, which OMP adds to what it tells the model. The same words for everyone, carried in the app. Rewritten at every start, and removed when both are off BrowserLink/: Null's copy of OMP's browser extension, under Null's name, which Chrome loads from here. Made when you set Chrome up Workspace/: Default working directory for conversations; not a filesystem access boundary Your own OMP settings are not modified. OMP owns the transcript and the credentials: a restart resumes the saved session, while /quit and idle Ctrl+C clear Null's pointer, not OMP's stored transcript, which /history finds again. A conversation you delete goes to the Mac's Trash. Logs are in ~/Library/Logs/Null/mini.log, and the smoke and self-test modes can log reply text, so keep sensitive prompts out of those checks.
